jobs.title: Asset Lifecycle Planning Director (Q - CO)
jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking an Asset Lifecycle Planning Director to join JASARA PMC. This role will establish the city-wide asset lifecycle planning framework, renewal rules and risk-based prioritization approach, integrating condition, risk, cost and performance data to shape lifecycle plans and renewal pipelines across portfolios.

The Asset Lifecycle Planning & Integration Director is accountable for establishing the city-wide lifecycle planning principles, frameworks, policies, renewal rules and intervention approach for City Asset Management. The role provides city-wide integration so lifecycle decisions across portfolios follow one unified ISO 55001-aligned AM framework, rather than fragmented local practices, and ensures decisions balance cost, risk, performance, service outcomes and whole-life asset value.

The role acts as the bridge between City AM portfolios and City Operations by defining lifecycle principles, intervention thresholds, maintenance policies, renewal criteria and cross-asset prioritization rules. It works with asset leads across the wider City AM team to ensure lifecycle plans reflect asset condition, criticality, hierarchy, service levels, O&M feedback and operational realities. It also works closely with the Enterprise AM Systems / SAP EAMS Director to ensure the AM platform and SAP EAMS produce the data, dashboards and decision-support outputs required to provide one trusted view of asset risk, condition, performance, backlog and lifecycle pressures across the city.

Key Responsibilities

1. Lifecycle Planning Framework, Principles and Policies

· Establish the city-wide asset lifecycle planning framework, principles, policies and governance approach for City AM, aligned to the AM Policy, AM Strategy and ISO 55001 principles.

· Define lifecycle planning standards that balance cost, risk, performance, service quality, safety, maintainability, resilience and long-term asset value.

· Set the approach for managing assets across their life, including how condition, criticality, hierarchy, risk, service levels and whole-life cost inform planning decisions.

· Develop renewal rules, intervention approaches, planning assumptions and decision criteria for assets across portfolios and districts.

· Set out consistent requirements for lifecycle plans, asset management plans, renewal pipelines, budget inputs and portfolio-level investment recommendations.

· Ensure lifecycle planning reflects agreed asset ownership boundaries, leasing arrangements, cost structures and links to capital and operating budget planning.

· Align lifecycle planning with operational readiness, handover, maintenance policies, SAP EAMS capabilities, AM governance and City Operations monitoring requirements.

2. Renewal Pipeline and Risk-Based Prioritisation

· Develop the city-wide lifecycle and renewal pipeline by joining condition, risk, cost, performance, criticality and maintenance data across portfolios.

· Prioritise assets coming into operation between 2026 and 2028, ensuring renewal needs, early-life risks and lifecycle obligations are visible before handover.

· Set risk-based prioritisation rules that guide when assets are maintained, monitored, refurbished, renewed, replaced or escalated for investment decision.

· Create practical rules for transferring lifecycle planning outputs and prioritisation logic to incoming City Operations resources once recruited.

· Ensure prioritisation decisions are transparent, evidence-based and auditable, supporting whole-life cost and value optimisation.

3. Intervention Thresholds and Maintenance Policy Integration

· Work with asset leads across the wider City AM team to define intervention thresholds, maintenance policies, inspection triggers and asset-specific lifecycle requirements.

· Ensure lifecycle planning reflects portfolio-specific asset behaviour, usage intensity, condition profiles, criticality, service impacts and operational constraints.

· Translate asset class requirements into consistent planning rules for renewals, planned maintenance, condition monitoring, deterioration assumptions and replacement strategies.

· Challenge proposed interventions where cost, risk, performance or lifecycle value are not sufficiently evidenced.

· Ensure maintenance and intervention policies remain aligned with operational readiness, O&M feedback, budget planning and long-term asset management objectives.

4. SAP EAMS and Data Integration for Lifecycle Planning

· Work with the Enterprise AM Systems / SAP EAMS Director to ensure the AM platform and SAP EAMS are ready to support lifecycle planning, renewal forecasting, intervention rules, condition scoring, risk prioritisation and cost-performance analysis.

· Define lifecycle data requirements, including asset hierarchy, classification, condition, criticality, failure modes, replacement value, expected life, maintenance history, cost, risk, performance and renewal information.

· Ensure dashboards and reports provide usable outputs for lifecycle forecasts, renewal pipelines, budget inputs, risk registers, backlog visibility, performance trends and portfolio decision-making.

· Link asset management outputs to financial reporting and work-management systems to support one version of the truth for lifecycle planning and investment decisions.

· Validate that data captured during handover and early operations is sufficient to support lifecycle planning, total cost of ownership, renewal prioritisation and adaptive change management.

· Promote a single source of lifecycle asset information that supports balanced decisions over the full lifespan of each asset.

5. Portfolio and Infrastructure Asset Integration

· Lead integration of lifecycle planning across asset portfolios, ensuring common AM standards while allowing asset-class specific intervention rules and maintenance policies.

· Direct the Asset Lifecycle & Costing Senior Manager to develop lifecycle cost models, renewal forecasts, budget inputs and whole-life cost analysis across asset portfolios.

· Direct the Infrastructure Assets Integration Manager to work with the Infrastructure portfolio lead on lifecycle plans and programmes for roads and car parks.

· Ensure risks, issues and opportunities from O&M are fed back into prioritisation, lifecycle plans, asset management plans and renewal pipelines.

· Coordinate with asset class leads to ensure lifecycle assumptions reflect operational realities, service expectations, deterioration patterns, usage intensity and maintenance strategy.

· Provide a city-wide integrated view of asset risk, performance, backlog and lifecycle pressures to inform capital and Opex planning.

· Support integrated planning across City AM so lifecycle, costing, risk, criticality, operational integration and infrastructure asset priorities are joined up across the city operating model.

6. Lifecycle Costing, Budget Inputs and Investment Planning

· Direct the Asset Lifecycle & Costing Senior Manager to develop lifecycle cost models, renewal forecasts, total cost of ownership analysis and portfolio-level budget inputs.

· Translate lifecycle plans into prioritised renewal programmes, multi-year capital requirements and operating budget implications.

· Ensure investment recommendations are supported by condition, risk, cost, criticality, performance, backlog and service-impact evidence.

· Support capital and Opex planning by identifying short-, medium- and long-term renewal needs, funding risks, deferral impacts and value optimisation options.

· Use KPI and trend reporting, performance monitoring and O&M feedback loops to refine lifecycle assumptions, renewal timing and maintenance strategies.

· Provide leadership reports on lifecycle cost exposure, renewal priorities, affordability constraints, risks, backlog and value-for-money options.

7. Stakeholder Interface and Handover to Operations

· Work closely with City Operations, O&M teams, asset class leads, governance and assurance teams, handover teams and SAP EAMS stakeholders to embed lifecycle requirements before assets become operational.

· Ensure lifecycle planning outputs are transferred into operational ownership, including renewal rules, intervention thresholds, prioritisation logic and known asset risks.

· Support handover to incoming City Operations resources once recruited, ensuring lifecycle planning methods and renewal pipeline ownership are clearly documented.

· Provide expert input into Stage Gate, readiness and handover processes where lifecycle, renewal or whole-life cost implications affect decisions.

· Ensure lifecycle risks, issues and opportunities are visible to leadership and reflected in asset management planning and governance forums.

8. Continuous Improvement and Lifecycle Policy Development

· Develop and continuously improve lifecycle planning policies, frameworks, templates, intervention logic, renewal rules, decision criteria and prioritisation methodologies.

· Use asset performance monitoring, condition data, risk trends, cost data, O&M feedback, lessons learned and SAP EAMS outputs to refine lifecycle assumptions and planning standards.

· Ensure lifecycle planning supports asset monitoring and continuous improvement, including cost, risk and asset health reporting, adaptive change management and lessons learned.

· Benchmark lifecycle planning approaches and promote consistency with ISO 55001-aligned asset management principles and relevant international good practice.

· Ensure lifecycle frameworks remain practical, scalable and usable by asset leads, O&M teams, portfolio teams and future City Operations resources.

· Build lifecycle planning capability across City AM through guidance, workshops, governance routines and clear decision-support tools.

Requirements

Education

· Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Asset Management, Cost and Performance balance, Operations Management, Facilities Management, Business Administration or a related discipline.

· Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred.

· Professional certification or membership in asset management, project management, data governance, SAP EAM or information management is desirable.

Experience

· Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in asset management, lifecycle planning, renewals, maintenance strategy, infrastructure operations, portfolio planning or asset investment planning, including senior leadership experience.

· Proven experience developing lifecycle planning frameworks, intervention policies, renewal rules, asset management plans and risk-based prioritisation approaches.

· Experience joining condition, risk, cost, performance and maintenance data to develop lifecycle forecasts, renewal pipelines and investment recommendations.

· Experience working with asset leads, O&M teams and enterprise asset management systems to define data requirements, intervention thresholds and decision-support outputs.

· Experience leading or directing lifecycle costing, infrastructure asset integration, roads, car parks, utilities, public realm, built environment or city operations portfolios.

· Experience in public sector, infrastructure, city operations, giga-projects, facilities management, transport, real estate or major destination environments is strongly preferred.

Preferred Background

· Background in lifecycle asset management, infrastructure asset management, maintenance strategy, renewals planning, capital planning, AM policy or portfolio-level asset investment planning.

· Practical exposure to ISO 55001 or ISO 55000-aligned asset management systems, including lifecycle value, risk-based decision-making, stakeholder requirements and continual improvement.

· Experience working across asset data, SAP EAMS/CMMS, O&M, finance, governance, handover and portfolio teams to turn lifecycle policy into operational and investment plans.

Technical & Functional Expectations

· Lifecycle planning frameworks, renewal rules, intervention thresholds, maintenance policies and asset management planning.

· Risk-based prioritisation, whole-life cost, cost-risk-performance trade-offs, value optimisation and investment planning.

· Condition, risk, cost, criticality, performance and maintenance data integration for lifecycle forecasting and renewal pipelines.

· SAP EAMS/CMMS lifecycle data requirements, dashboards, reports and decision-support outputs.

· Infrastructure asset lifecycle planning, roads, car parks, O&M feedback loops and portfolio integration.

· ISO 55001-aligned asset management principles, lifecycle value, risk management and continual improvement.

jobs.title: Community Inspector - CITY AM
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Community Inspector is responsible for conducting routine inspections across residential and mixed-use communities to ensure compliance with community rules, municipal regulations, health and safety standards, and property management requirements. The role focuses on maintaining community appearance, resident satisfaction, and operational excellence by identifying, reporting, and following up on violations and maintenance issues.

Key Responsibilities

Community Inspections

  • Conduct regular inspections of residential, commercial, and common areas within the community.
  • Identify violations related to community rules, property standards, landscaping, parking, waste management, and public safety.
  • Monitor community facilities, amenities, and infrastructure to ensure they are maintained to required standards.
  • Report defects, damages, and maintenance requirements to relevant departments.

Compliance Monitoring

  • Ensure compliance with community management policies, municipal regulations, and environmental standards.
  • Inspect contractor activities to verify adherence to approved standards and safety requirements.
  • Document violations and initiate corrective action procedures.
  • Follow up on outstanding violations and ensure timely resolution.

Resident & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Respond to resident complaints and service requests related to community conditions.
  • Provide guidance to residents and tenants regarding community regulations and standards.
  • Coordinate with property management teams, maintenance contractors, and external authorities when required.

Reporting & Documentation

  • Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly inspection reports.
  • Maintain accurate records of inspections, findings, violations, and corrective actions.
  • Use inspection software, mobile applications, or property management systems to record observations and track resolutions.
  • Generate photographic evidence and detailed reports for management review.

Health, Safety & Environmental Monitoring

  • Identify potential health and safety hazards within the community.
  • Ensure public areas are clean, safe, and accessible.
  • Monitor waste disposal practices and environmental compliance.
  • Report emergency situations and support incident investigations when necessary.

Qualifications

  • Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Property Management, Civil Engineering, Urban Planning, or a related field.
  • Professional certifications in Property Management, Facilities Management, or Health & Safety are an advantage.

Experience

  • 2-5 years of experience in community management, facilities management, property inspection, municipal inspection, or related fields.
  • Experience within residential communities, mixed-use developments, hospitality destinations, or real estate projects preferred.

jobs.description:

We are seeking a Director of Waste to join JASARA PMC. The Director – Waste Management provides strategic asset management leadership for City’s integrated waste management portfolio, ensuring waste assets, infrastructure, systems, service models, and commercial arrangements are planned, governed, optimised, and assured across the full asset lifecycle. The role defines the long-term strategy, value framework, lifecycle standards, investment requirements, regulatory assurance model, and performance management approach required to enable safe, sustainable, cost-effective, and future-ready waste management services at city scale.

The Director is accountable for developing and governing a circular, digitally enabled, and commercially robust waste asset management system covering municipal solid waste, recyclables, organics, construction and demolition waste, event waste, hazardous waste, special waste streams, transfer stations, treatment facilities, recycling infrastructure, digital platforms, and final disposal interfaces.

The role sets the strategic direction for waste asset planning, lifecycle investment, asset information, service procurement strategy, operational readiness assurance, risk management, stakeholder alignment, resource recovery, and continuous improvement, ensuring alignment with asset management framework, sustainability ambitions, Saudi regulatory requirements, Vision 2030 priorities, and international best practice.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Leadership, Governance & Operating Model

· Own waste governance frameworks, policies, technical standards, procedures, assurance controls, and performance reporting.

· Translate sustainability, ESG, circular economy, and smart city ambitions into practical waste management programmes.

· Provide executive-level recommendations, decision papers, business cases, risk reports, and performance dashboards.

· Ensure waste management requirements are embedded into master planning, design reviews, asset handover, operations readiness, and event planning.

 2. Waste Asset Strategy, Planning & Service Model

· Lead strategic options analysis for future service models, including in-house capability, outsourced providers, framework contracts, concessions, public-private partnerships, and integrated city-wide service platforms.

· Establish waste asset planning requirements for new developments, precincts, venues, events, hospitality zones, retail areas, public realm, residential communities, and back-of-house logistics corridors.

· Set standards for asset design, maintainability, operability, safe access, storage capacity, segregation infrastructure, collection interfaces, transfer facilities, treatment interfaces, and digital connectivity.

· Develop lifecycle investment plans covering renewal, replacement, upgrade, expansion, obsolescence, risk mitigation, technology refresh, and resilience improvements across the waste asset portfolio.

· Ensure waste asset strategies are integrated with facilities management, utilities, transport, logistics, real estate, sustainability, development delivery, HSE, security, events, and commercial planning functions.

· Provide strategic assurance that proposed assets, systems, contracts, and service models remain fit for purpose across phased opening, growth, peak demand periods, and long-term operating horizon.

3. Sustainability, Circular Economy & Resource Value Strategy

· Define waste hierarchy strategy, circular economy roadmap, and resource value framework, prioritising prevention, reduction, reuse, segregation, recycling, recovery, and responsible disposal.

· Develop material flow strategies for municipal solid waste, recyclables, organics, food waste, construction and demolition waste, hazardous waste, event waste, landscape waste, and special waste streams.

· Set long-term diversion, recovery, contamination reduction, reuse, carbon reduction, and circularity targets aligned with ESG commitments, Vision 2030 priorities, Saudi regulations, and international best practice.

· Identify strategic resource recovery opportunities, including recycling markets, organics processing, composting, anaerobic digestion, waste-to-energy, material recovery facilities, reverse logistics, and producer responsibility partnerships.

· Lead business case development for circular economy infrastructure, assessing whole-life cost, environmental benefits, commercial returns, regulatory implications, technology maturity, land requirements, and operational interfaces.

· Establish policies, standards, and performance requirements for segregation at source, tenant waste management, public realm recycling, event waste planning, construction waste recovery, and contractor reporting.

· Create mechanisms to track resource value, including recovered material volumes, avoided disposal cost, revenue potential, carbon impact, contamination levels, market demand, and contribution to sustainability reporting.

· Partner with development, procurement, commercial, design, tenant management, events, hospitality, and sustainability teams to embed circular economy principles into assets, leases, vendor requirements, and operating standards.

· Provide strategic advice on emerging waste technologies, policy changes, circular economy partnerships, innovation pilots, and investment opportunities that improve long-term resource productivity and environmental outcomes.

4. Asset Information, Smart Systems & Digital Strategy

· Define the waste asset information strategy, ensuring all assets, systems, facilities, equipment, digital devices, service interfaces, and treatment/disposal links are captured within a structured asset register and aligned to the enterprise asset management framework.

· Establish data standards for asset hierarchy, location, ownership, condition, criticality, lifecycle status, capacity, performance, maintenance strategy, warranty, risk, cost, and compliance attributes.

· Develop requirements for GIS mapping, spatial asset data, precinct-level waste infrastructure mapping, collection point visibility, transfer station interfaces, treatment facility data, and integration with city-wide planning systems.

· Set the strategic roadmap for smart waste technologies, including IoT-enabled bins and compactors, fill-level sensors, weighbridge systems, RFID tagging, route optimisation, fleet telematics, smart collection points, and automated reporting tools.

· Define integration requirements between waste systems, enterprise asset management platforms, CAFM/CMMS systems, ERP, command centre platforms, digital twin environments, sustainability dashboards, and regulatory reporting systems.

· Create dashboards and performance intelligence requirements covering asset availability, utilisation, condition, lifecycle risk, service demand, waste generation, diversion, contamination, contractor performance, cost-to-serve, and carbon impact.

· Use data analytics to support strategic decisions on asset renewal, service model optimisation, investment prioritisation, demand forecasting, capacity planning, technology deployment, risk mitigation, and circular economy performance.

· Establish data governance controls, including data ownership, quality assurance, validation routines, change control, audit trails, reporting cadence, cybersecurity considerations, and minimum data requirements for contractors and developers.

· Ensure digital requirements are embedded in design briefs, procurement specifications, contracts, handover packages, commissioning plans, operating procedures, and lifecycle information requirements.

· Promote insight-led asset management by converting operational data, service trends, technology outputs, customer feedback, regulatory requirements, and sustainability metrics into strategic improvement plans and investment recommendations.

5. Authority & Regulatory Compliance

· Ensure compliance with Saudi environmental regulations and waste management laws.

· Act as senior interface with regulators, competent authorities, developers, operators, contractors, and strategic partners including:

Ø  National Center for Waste Management (MWAN)

Ø  Ministry of Environment, Water & Agriculture (MEWA)

Ø  Local municipalities and regulatory authorities

· Oversee compliance assurance for:

Ø  Permits and licensing

Ø  Environmental audits and reporting

Ø  Hazardous waste handling compliance

6. Asset Lifecycle Management & Infrastructure Strategy

· Develop and govern strategic asset management plans for waste infrastructure, including transfer stations, recycling facilities, treatment assets, storage areas, compactors, collection points, hazardous waste facilities, fleet interfaces, digital systems, and disposal/treatment partnerships.

· Define lifecycle strategies for each major waste asset class, covering planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, mobilisation, operation, maintenance, renewal, upgrade, repurposing, decommissioning, and end-of-life transition.

· Establish asset criticality and risk frameworks to prioritise investment, maintenance strategy, redundancy, resilience, contingency planning, spare capacity, and service continuity for high-impact waste assets and interfaces.

· Set condition assessment, inspection, performance monitoring, defect classification, failure mode, and asset health requirements to inform lifecycle planning and evidence-based asset decisions.

· Develop renewal and replacement programmes based on asset age, condition, utilisation, criticality, regulatory requirements, technology obsolescence, service demand, safety risk, environmental performance, and whole-life cost.

· Ensure infrastructure strategy considers phased city growth, peak visitor demand, major event loading, precinct expansion, seasonal variation, emergency scenarios, contractor capacity, transport interfaces, and future regulatory or sustainability requirements.

· Define maintainability, accessibility, operability, safety-by-design, environmental control, odour management, leachate management, traffic movement, segregation, storage, and collection interface requirements for new and existing waste assets.

· Lead strategic input into design reviews, technical specifications, employer requirements, asset acceptance criteria, commissioning standards, handover documentation, as-built records, O&M manuals, warranties, spares, and training requirements.

· Provide assurance that assets handed over from development projects are complete, registered, compliant, maintainable, digitally captured, commercially supportable, and aligned with agreed levels of service and lifecycle strategies.

· Shape infrastructure investment cases by evaluating capacity constraints, service risks, environmental impact, technology options, land requirements, interface dependencies, capital cost, operating cost, lifecycle risk, and long-term asset value.

· Embed ISO 55001 principles into waste asset governance, including value alignment, risk-based decision-making, lifecycle thinking, asset information quality, continual improvement, and clear accountability for asset outcomes.

· Maintain a long-term infrastructure roadmap that identifies required asset interventions, capacity upgrades, resilience improvements, technology refresh cycles, renewal priorities, funding needs, and strategic dependencies across project operating horizon.

7. Health, Safety & Environment (HSE)

· Ensure safe handling of all waste streams, including hazardous materials

· Enforce HSE standards, PPE compliance, and safe systems of work

· Manage environmental risks such as:

Ø  Leachate control

8. Commercial Strategy, Investment Planning & Provider Governance

· Own the commercial and investment strategy for waste assets, services, procurement packages, lifecycle cost planning, value optimisation, and budget governance.

· Develop sourcing strategies, service delivery models, make-versus-buy assessments, concession opportunities, and performance-based contract structures.

9. Stakeholder Engagement & Public Awareness

Ø  Event organisers

· Promote community participation in sustainability initiatives

10. Executive Leadership, Organisation Capability & Culture

Requirements

The Director serves as the commercial Subject Matter Expert (SME), providing strategic guidance on contracting strategies, supplier performance, commercial negotiations, cost management, and contract assurance to support safe, reliable, and cost-effective utility operations.

  • Ensure compliance with organizational procurement and contracting requirements.

  • Ensure procurement activities achieve best value while maintaining quality and compliance.

jobs.title: DLP Snagging Professional (Q - CO)
jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking a DLP Snagging Professional to join JASARA PMC. The DLP & Snagging Professional is responsible for supporting the identification, coordination, tracking, and close-out of defects, snags, and Defects Liability Period (DLP) obligations across assigned Qiddiya City assets. The role works closely with project teams, consultants, contractors, service providers, and operational stakeholders to ensure defects are recorded, monitored, and progressed to closure in accordance with contractual requirements, operational standards, and handover processes. The position contributes to asset handover, operational readiness, and the successful transition of assets into operational use.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support day-to-day DLP and snagging activities across assigned assets, ensuring identified defects and incomplete works are accurately logged and tracked through to resolution.
  • Participate in inspections, joint walkthroughs, snagging reviews, defect verification visits, and close-out assessments with project teams, consultants, contractors, and operational stakeholders.
  • Maintain defect and snag registers, ensuring records include ownership, priority, target dates, status updates, supporting evidence, and close-out documentation.
  • Monitor progress of defect rectification works and follow up with contractors and service providers to ensure closure within agreed timelines.
  • Assist in reviewing handover documentation, including O&M manuals, warranties, asset registers, testing and commissioning records, training documentation, and defect close-out records.
  • Update CAFM/CMMS systems, snagging platforms, dashboards, and reporting tools to ensure accurate defect tracking and status reporting.
  • Support the assessment of defects for potential impacts on safety, compliance, asset reliability, maintainability, operational performance, and customer experience.
  • Coordinate with internal teams including facilities management, infrastructure, utilities, landscaping, public realm, security, and project delivery teams to support defect resolution and interface management.
  • Contribute to readiness reviews, defect reporting, contractor performance monitoring, warranty tracking, and lessons learned activities.
  • Prepare reports, maintain records, and provide progress updates on outstanding defects, rectification activities, and DLP performance metrics

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Engineering, Facilities Management, Construction Management, Building Services, Asset Management, or a related discipline.
  • With 7-10 years of experience in construction completion, asset handover, DLP administration, snagging, facilities management, operations readiness, or maintenance environments.
  • Experience coordinating with contractors, consultants, and service providers on defect rectification, inspections, close-out activities, and warranty management.
  • Experience within large-scale developments, mixed-use communities, infrastructure assets, public realm environments, or similar operational environments is desirable.

jobs.title: Road network engineer - City Ops O&M

Job Summary

The Road Network Engineer is responsible for the planning, design, operation, and maintenance assessment of road networks within urban developments, communities, cities, and large-scale infrastructure projects. Road Network Planning & Design

  • Develop road network strategies and transportation infrastructure plans.
  • Review and evaluate road layouts, alignments, intersections, and access points.
  • Ensure road designs comply with local and international engineering standards.
  • Assess road hierarchy, connectivity, and capacity requirements for current and future demand.
  • Support master planning activities and infrastructure integration.

Traffic Engineering & Analysis

  • Conduct traffic studies, transportation assessments, and capacity analyses.
  • Analyze traffic volumes, flow patterns, congestion points, and network performance.
  • Identify bottlenecks and recommend infrastructure improvements.
  • Support transportation demand management initiatives.
  • Evaluate road network performance using simulation and modeling tools.

Road Safety & Compliance

  • Conduct road safety audits and inspections.
  • Identify safety risks, accident-prone locations, and operational deficiencies.
  • Recommend measures to improve road safety, signage, pavement markings, and traffic control systems.
  • Ensure compliance with municipal, transportation authority, and regulatory requirements.

Infrastructure Performance Monitoring

  • Monitor road network performance through data collection and analysis.
  • Evaluate pavement conditions, road asset functionality, and maintenance requirements.
  • Coordinate with maintenance teams to prioritize repairs and upgrades.
  • Develop performance reports and recommendations for continuous improvement.

Smart Mobility & Transportation Systems

  • Support implementation of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS).
  • Evaluate traffic management technologies and smart mobility solutions.
  • Coordinate integration of road infrastructure with public transportation, cycling, and pedestrian networks.
  • Support initiatives related to sustainable transportation and future mobility.

Stakeholder Coordination

  • Coordinate with government authorities, consultants, contractors, and utility providers.
  • Review engineering submissions, technical reports, and design packages.
  • Participate in project meetings and provide technical guidance.
  • Support project delivery from planning through construction and operation phases.

Reporting & Documentation

  • Prepare technical reports, traffic assessments, and engineering recommendations.
  • Maintain records of road network studies, inspections, and improvement initiatives.
  • Present findings and recommendations to management and stakeholders.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Highway Engineering, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Transportation Engineering is an advantage.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) registration or equivalent certification is preferred.

Experience

  • 4-8 years of experience in road design, transportation planning, traffic engineering, or highway infrastructure projects.
  • Experience with urban developments, smart cities, transportation networks, or large-scale infrastructure projects.
  • Experience working with government authorities, municipalities, or engineering consultancies is preferred.

jobs.title: SAP-EAMS Director (Q-CO)
jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking an SAP-EAMS Director to join JASARA PMC. This role will lead enterprise asset management systems, SAP EAMS readiness and asset data governance, working across City Operations, City AM, Asset Class BUs and O&M teams to create a trusted single source of asset information.

The Enterprise Asset Management Director is accountable for leading the city’s enterprise asset management systems, asset information governance and SAP EAMS preparation within the City Asset Management organisation. The role works closely with City Operations, the wider AM team, Asset Class BUs, O&M teams, handover, digital, finance and governance functions to ensure asset information, operational requirements and AM standards are aligned across the city operating model from an AM point of view.

The position acts as the business owner for SAP EAMS design decisions, data migration standards, process integration and reporting requirements, ensuring the platform enables reliable operations, lifecycle planning, maintenance delivery, service-quality monitoring and investment decision-making. It embeds the AM data model, workflows, KPIs and reporting framework so City Operations, portfolios and O&M teams have one trusted source of asset information and a consistent approach to asset performance, lifecycle and renewals planning.

Key Responsibilities

1. Enterprise AM Systems Strategy and Governance

· Define and maintain the enterprise asset management systems strategy, roadmap, governance framework and operating model for City AM and City Operations.

· Act as business owner for SAP EAMS design decisions, ensuring system configuration reflects approved AM policies, lifecycle processes, service-quality standards, operational requirements and governance controls.

· Align AM systems, asset data standards and reporting outputs with portfolio priorities, asset intersections and operational requirements that support integrated city planning.

· Establish clear decision rights, escalation routes and accountabilities across City AM, City Operations, O&M, Asset Class BUs, Digital, Finance, Procurement, Handover and governance teams.

· Lead standards for asset information ownership, configuration control, system access, master data stewardship and change control.

· Provide executive advice, options, risks, cost implications and recommendations on enterprise AM systems, data quality, SAP EAMS readiness and city-wide AM integration.

2. SAP EAMS Preparation, Cut-over and Integration

· Lead business preparation and cut-over to SAP EAMS, including readiness planning, business acceptance criteria, cut-over sequencing, issue management and early-life support arrangements.

· Define business requirements for SAP EAMS configuration, workflows, asset structures, maintenance processes, user roles, dashboards and reporting outputs.

· Set data migration standards, validation rules, reconciliation controls and sign-off processes for asset master data, hierarchy, location, ownership, condition, performance, maintenance and lifecycle information.

· Ensure SAP EAMS integrates with existing AM processes, City Operations dashboards, portfolio reporting, handover controls, maintenance planning, finance inputs and operational support requirements.

·       Embed data and workflow requirements needed to support business-as-usual AM changes, capacity increases, readiness impacts, commercialisation inputs and service-charge information for relevant assets.

·       Coordinate design reviews, user acceptance testing, mock cut-overs, defect resolution and go-live readiness decisions with Digital, City Operations and implementation partners.

3. AM Data Model, Asset Register and Information Standards

·       Define and embed the enterprise AM data model, including asset classification, hierarchy, location structure, ownership attributes, criticality, condition, lifecycle status and maintenance master data.

·       Own the standards for the central asset register so asset information is accurate, complete, consistent and usable across districts, portfolios, systems and asset types.

·       Establish data quality controls, validation checks, cleansing routines, reconciliation processes and exception reporting to identify and resolve data gaps.

·       Ensure asset data requirements are embedded into handover, adoption, acceptance and configuration management processes.

·       Lead audits, assurance reviews and governance reporting on asset information quality, system compliance and register completeness.

4. Workflows, KPIs and Reporting Standards

·       Define and embed AM workflows in SAP EAMS for asset creation, updates, approvals, maintenance planning, inspections, renewals, defects, work orders and lifecycle interventions.

·       Set standard KPIs, reporting definitions, dashboard requirements and performance measures for asset condition, reliability, maintenance compliance, data quality and lifecycle cost visibility.

·       Ensure portfolios and O&M teams use consistent reporting standards and a common source of asset information for decision-making.

·       Work with Digital and reporting teams to produce standard dashboards, data extracts and management packs for operational, compliance, planning and executive governance forums.

·       Use reporting outputs to identify systemic issues, improvement opportunities and process refinements across AM processes and systems.

5. Change, Training and User Adoption

·       Coordinate business change, communications, training and adoption activities so users understand new processes, system roles and data responsibilities.

·       Develop role-based training requirements, user guidance, process maps, job aids and adoption support for Asset Management, O&M, portfolio and governance users.

·       Lead early-life support after go-live, ensuring user issues, data defects and process gaps are quickly triaged, resolved and fed back into future updates.

6. Stakeholder, Portfolio and O&M Interface

·       Partner with City Operations, portfolio leaders, Asset Class BUs, district teams, O&M teams, handover, technical authorities and service providers to ensure asset information supports practical operational needs.

·       Align portfolio priorities, asset intersections and operational requirements so SAP EAMS and AM reporting support integrated planning and city-wide coordination.

·       Coordinate asset data requirements for maintenance schedules, inspection regimes, renewals planning, compliance obligations, budget decisions, capacity assumptions and visitor demand planning.

·       Support visibility of asset go-live timelines, readiness status, operator arrangements, asset governance standards and interface requirements ahead of asset opening or major events.

·       Enable consistent asset performance, lifecycle and service-quality standards by incorporating operational insights on condition, utilisation, performance gaps, asset risks and renewal needs.

·       Coordinate with City Operations and wider AM stakeholders on asset ownership boundaries, commercialisation opportunities, service-charge inputs and value optimisation priorities where these affect City Ops-managed or city-facing assets.

·       Facilitate cross-functional workshops to align system design, process ownership, data standards, reporting requirements and post-opening lessons learned across the city operating model.

7. Continuous Improvement and System Enhancement

·       Own the AM systems improvement backlog, prioritising enhancements based on operational value, risk reduction, compliance needs and user feedback.

·       Monitor system adoption, data quality trends, workflow performance and reporting effectiveness to drive continual improvement.

·       Ensure lessons learned from SAP EAMS cut-over, early-life support, audits and operational use are converted into improved standards, training and system updates.

·       Promote standardisation, automation and data-led decision-making across the asset lifecycle.

8. Commercial, Supplier and Implementation Partner Management

·       Develop scopes, deliverables, acceptance criteria and performance requirements for AM systems, data governance, SAP EAMS implementation and reporting support.

·       Manage consultants, implementation partners and system support providers to ensure deliverables are practical, integrated and aligned with City Operations requirements.

·       Review supplier outputs, design documents, test evidence, migration plans, training materials and reporting products for business usability and quality.

·       Own assigned budgets, forecasts, procurement inputs, contract performance and value-for-money initiatives.

Ensure supplier recommendations are translated into sustainable internal capability, governance routines and operational

Requirements

Education

·       Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Asset Management, Information Systems, Operations Management, Facilities Management, Business Administration or a related discipline.

·       Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred.

·       Professional certification or membership in asset management, project management, data governance, SAP EAM or information management is desirable.

jobs.title: Senior Director - Event Mobility Planning (Q - CO)
jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking a Senior Director - Event Mobility Planning to join JASARA PMC. The Senior Director, Event Mobility Planning is accountable for establishing and leading the integrated mobility planning capability for major events, festivals, sporting competitions and entertainment activations across the city program. The role ensures the safe, efficient and coordinated movement of guests, athletes, performers, VIPs, workforce, volunteers, logistics vehicles, emergency services and public transport users across venues, districts and transport modes.

The position acts as the City Operations mobility lead and coordination authority for major events. It develops citywide standards, demand forecasts, event mobility plans, traffic management plans and operational readiness arrangements particularly for city’s major events programme in 2028, while maintaining clear boundaries with venue and asset operators that remain accountable for operations within their controlled areas.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategy, Governance and Function Leadership

·   Develop, maintain and implement the Programme Event Mobility Strategy, governance framework, operating model, standards, policies and planning calendar.

·   Create a scalable mobility capability covering business-as-usual destination operations, recurring events, overlapping event programmes and major-event overlays.

·   Define clear accountabilities, decision rights, escalation routes and interfaces across City Operations, districts, venues, transport operators, security, emergency services and government stakeholders.

·   Lead the permanent mobility planning team and mobilise specialist consultants, service providers and temporary event resources as required.

·   Provide executive advice, decision papers, options, risk assessments, cost implications and recommendations on event mobility matters.

2. Integrated Event Mobility Planning

·   Lead the development, assurance and approval of integrated Event Mobility Plans for the full event lifecycle, from concept and feasibility through readiness, live delivery and post-event review.

·   Convert event attendance profiles, venue capacities, session schedules and origin-destination assumptions into transport demand forecasts, mode-share targets and time-phased arrival and departure plans.

·   Plan distinct mobility journeys for general admission guests, hospitality customers, VIPs, athletes, performers, officials, workforce, volunteers, media, people of determination and emergency responders.

·   Coordinate mobility plans across simultaneous events to manage cumulative demand, shared infrastructure, operational conflicts and network resilience.

·   Maintain an integrated mobility planning schedule with defined submissions, reviews, approvals, exercises and operational handover gates.

3. Traffic, Access and Parking Planning

·   Oversee Traffic Management Plans, road network assessments, access-control strategies, temporary traffic management, diversions, closures, pick-up and drop-off areas and emergency access routes.

·   Develop event parking strategies covering pre-booked parking, park-and-ride, VIP and hospitality allocation, workforce parking, accessible parking, overflow arrangements and parking technology.

·   Ensure vehicle access, accreditation and permit arrangements align with security zoning, venue ingress and egress, logistics windows and public-realm requirements.

·   Use modelling, scenario testing and live operational data to validate assumptions and optimise road, kerbside and parking capacity.

4. Public Transport, Shuttle and Active Mobility Integration

·   Design integrated bus, shuttle, public transport, taxi and ride-hailing service plans with clear capacities, frequencies, staging, layover, dispatch, queuing and passenger information requirements.

·   Coordinate park-and-ride and remote transport hub operations, including fleet sizing, boarding processes, accessibility, contingency vehicles and demand management.

·   Integrate walking, micromobility and last-mile routes with venue, public-realm, wayfinding, crowd management and accessibility plans.

·   Agree service levels, operational interfaces and recovery arrangements with mobility operators and delivery partners.

5. VIP, Hospitality and Specialist Movements

·   Develop secure, discreet and service-led mobility plans for Royal, government, VIP, sponsor, hospitality and protocol movements.

·   Coordinate premium ground transport, coach, chauffeur, charter and aviation interfaces where required, in partnership with security, protocol and specialist providers.

·   Establish holding, dispatch, route, access, parking and contingency arrangements that protect both guest experience and network performance.

6. Logistics and Operational Interface

·   Integrate freight, servicing, waste, catering, retail, broadcast and contractor movements with the guest mobility plan to minimise conflicts and maintain operational continuity.

·   Coordinate delivery routes, vehicle staging, holding areas, time windows, access permits and back-of-house interfaces with the City Logistics function and venue operators.

·   Ensure emergency service routes and incident response access are protected throughout build, event and breakdown phases.

7. Operational Readiness and Live Event Delivery

·   Lead mobility readiness reviews, tabletop exercises, simulations, test events, route proving and operational rehearsals.

·   Define mobility command, control, communications, reporting and escalation arrangements, including integration with the City Command and Control Unit and relevant event control rooms.

·   Provide senior mobility leadership during live operations, ensuring timely decisions, coordinated issue resolution and deployment of contingency measures.

·   Lead structured post-event reviews, capture lessons learned and ensure corrective actions are incorporated into future plans and standards.

8. Stakeholder, Commercial and Supplier Management

·   Build effective working relationships with transport authorities, traffic police, emergency services, public transport operators, districts, venues, hotels, event organisers, service providers and relevant government entities.

·   Lead multi-agency mobility workshops, design reviews, readiness forums and executive reporting.

·   Develop scopes, procurement strategies and performance requirements for mobility planning, modelling, technology and event delivery services.

·   Ensure suppliers are appropriately qualified, locally compliant and capable of mobilising suitable Saudi-based resources and workforce development plans.

·   Own assigned budgets, forecasts, commercial evaluations, contract performance and value-for-money initiatives.

Requirements

Education

·   Bachelor's degree in Transport Planning, Civil or Transportation Engineering, Urban Planning, Logistics, Operations Management or a related discipline.

·   Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred.

·   Professional membership or certification in transport planning, traffic engineering, project management, event management or a related field is desirable.

Experience

·   Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in transport planning, mobility operations, traffic engineering, major event transport (FIFA World Cup or Olympics), city operations or major infrastructure, including at least 8 years in senior leadership roles.

jobs.title: Senior Director - Land & Public Realm Optimisation - Land Use (Q - CO)
jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking a Senior Director, Land & Public Realm Optimisation - Land Use to join JASARA PMC. The Senior Director, Land & Public Realm Optimisation is accountable for supporting City Operations in reviewing proposed city land and public realm before it is accepted or vested into the City Operations portfolio. The role assesses parks, landscaped areas, plazas, civic spaces, pedestrian areas, green corridors, recreational open spaces and other proposed public land to determine whether each area is genuinely public, operationally necessary, appropriately sized, cost-efficient and financially sustainable throughout its lifecycle.

The position acts as City Operations’ independent challenge and assurance function. It provides evidence-based recommendations to the Executive Director, City Operations, and relevant governance forums on whether proposed land should be accepted, conditionally accepted, redesigned, reduced, retained by the benefiting developer or asset owner, placed under an alternative management arrangement, or not vested to City Operations.

Key Responsibilities

1. Land and Public Realm Governance

·   Develop and maintain the City Operations Land and Public Realm Vesting Framework, including review criteria, evidence requirements, stage gates, approval routes and decision records.

·   Establish consistent standards for determining public purpose, operational need, affordability, maintainability and ownership responsibility.

·   Ensure proposed land is not assumed to be a City Operations liability solely because it is externally accessible or shown as public realm in a masterplan.

·   Provide formal recommendations and executive decision papers on acceptance, conditional acceptance, redesign, alternative ownership or rejection.

2. Public Purpose and Beneficiary Assessment

·   Assess whether proposed land is genuinely public in purpose, access, use and benefit.

·   Determine whether the primary beneficiaries are the wider city and community or an adjacent private development, hotel, resort, residential community, venue, attraction or commercial asset.

·   Challenge public designations that do not align with the intended user base, access arrangements or operational reality.

·   Recommend that land primarily benefiting private assets remains owned, funded or maintained by the benefiting party while protecting any agreed public-access obligations.

3. Land Area and Functional Need Review

·   Review the scale, location, configuration, boundaries and intended use of parks and other proposed public realm.

·   Assess whether land area is proportionate to forecast demand, public value and demonstrated operational need.

·   Challenge oversized, duplicated, fragmented, inaccessible, residual or low-utilisation public spaces.

·   Identify opportunities to consolidate public realm into fewer, better-performing spaces that provide stronger public value at lower lifecycle cost.

·   Ensure proposed spaces have a clear function, target user, operating concept and measurable benefit.

4. Parks, Open Space and Public Realm Review

·   Lead City Operations reviews of public parks, neighbourhood and destination parks, landscaped open areas, urban plazas, civic spaces, pedestrian areas, public squares, green corridors, recreational open spaces and publicly accessible landscaped land.

·   Assess intended use, forecast demand, opening hours, accessibility, safety, security, thermal comfort, amenities, seasonal use, event potential and long-term renewal needs.

·   Review landscape intensity, irrigation demand, water use, cleaning, waste, pest control, security patrol, staffing, supervision and maintenance access implications.

·   Challenge over-designed or maintenance-intensive solutions where simpler alternatives can maintain quality, accessibility and guest experience.

5. Whole-Life Cost and Affordability

·   Establish a consistent methodology for assessing the whole-life cost of proposed land and public realm.

·   Prepare or assure annual and long-term cost forecasts covering landscape maintenance, irrigation, water, cleaning, waste, security, pest control, amenities, furniture, play equipment, lighting within public spaces, staffing, technology and periodic renewal.

·   Compare forecast public value and utilisation with the operating and renewal liability proposed for City Operations.

·   Identify avoidable cost drivers and recommend redesign, scope reduction, funding contributions or alternative management arrangements where costs are disproportionate.

·   Maintain clear cost assumptions to support City Operations budget, workforce and service planning.

6. Operational Suitability and Maintainability

·   Assess whether proposed parks and public spaces can be safely, practically and efficiently operated.

·   Review access for cleaning, waste collection, landscape maintenance, security patrols, servicing and emergency response.

·   Identify isolated, concealed, inaccessible or difficult-to-supervise areas and unclear public/private boundaries.

·   Assess whether landscaping, amenities and materials are suitable for the climate, anticipated use and available maintenance regime.

·   Recommend design changes that improve usability and reduce cost without undermining public benefit, inclusion or quality.

7. Vesting Recommendations and Conditions

·   Issue clear recommendations to accept, accept subject to conditions, defer pending evidence, redesign or reduce, retain under developer or asset-owner control, adopt a shared model, or reject from the City Operations portfolio.

·   Define conditions relating to boundary clarification, design amendments, cost reduction, maintenance funding, service charges, endowments, developer maintenance periods, performance guarantees, public access, handover standards and defect rectification.

·   Confirm that agreed conditions and required evidence are closed before final acceptance or handover.

·   Maintain an auditable record of recommendations, decisions, conditions, owners and close-out status.

8. Ownership, Funding and Management Options

·   Evaluate alternatives to direct vesting, including private ownership with public access, developer-managed public realm, district management, shared maintenance, service-charge recovery, sponsorship, commercial activation, concession or destination-management arrangements.

·   Ensure alternative models protect public access, service quality, affordability and clear accountability.

·   Prevent City Operations from assuming costs that should reasonably remain with the principal beneficiary.

·   Support commercial and legal teams in defining practical ownership, funding and management obligations.

9. Land and Public Realm Portfolio Register

·   Establish and maintain a citywide register of proposed and accepted public land, recording area, use, beneficiaries, ownership, vesting status, annual operating cost, renewal exposure, risks, funding, conditions and responsible party.

·   Use the register to identify cumulative cost and workforce exposure across districts and development phases.

·   Provide executive dashboards on land under review, contested proposals, avoided liabilities, conditional acceptances and future budget exposure.

·   Support long-term city land optimisation by identifying opportunities to consolidate, reclassify or change management arrangements for underperforming public realm.

10. Stakeholder Coordination and Team Leadership

·   Lead structured reviews with masterplanning, development, design, landscape architecture, district teams, asset owners, Finance, Commercial, Legal, Governance and City Operations service functions.

·   Provide early operational input before land boundaries and designs become fixed or commercial commitments are made.

·   Resolve disagreements concerning public purpose, ownership boundaries, cost and operating responsibility, escalating unresolved issues with evidence and options.

·   Build and lead a specialist team, supported where required by landscape, cost, land, commercial and operational advisors.

·  Develop internal guidance and capability so affordability and maintainability are embedded across the development lifecycle.

Requirements

Education

·   Bachelor's degree in Urban Planning, Landscape Architecture, Real Estate, Land Economics, Asset Management, Facilities Management, Environmental Design or a related discipline.

·   Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred.

·   Professional membership in planning, landscape architecture, real estate, asset management or facilities management is desirable.

Experience

·   Minimum 20 years of progressive experience in land-use planning, public realm, parks and open-space planning, landscape planning, real estate, asset management or city operations, including at least 8 years in senior leadership or advisory roles.

·   Demonstrable experience reviewing parks, public spaces, landscaped areas or major-destination public realm.

·   Strong experience assessing operating costs, maintenance implications and whole-life liabilities and translating findings into business cases and executive recommendations.

·   Proven ability to challenge land, design, ownership or funding proposals based on public purpose, operational need, affordability and maintainability.

·   Experience in Saudi Arabia, the GCC, major destination developments or giga-project environments is strongly preferred.

Preferred Background

·   Experience within a development authority, city or municipal organisation, major destination, integrated resort, public-realm consultancy, real-estate developer or asset-management organisation.

·   Practical exposure to land vesting, public/private boundary definition, parks operations, landscape maintenance, service-charge models and developer handover.

·   Experience working across planning, design, operations, finance, commercial, legal and governance disciplines.

jobs.description:
Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments.

We are seeking a Service Charge Director to join JASARA PMC. The role responsibility is own the city-wide service charge framework, governance and operating model, ensuring service charges, cost recovery mechanisms and revenue opportunities are consistently identified, evaluated, governed and aligned with City Operations, Asset Management and district operating requirements.

The Service Charges & Revenue Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining the city-wide service charge framework, governance model, charging methodologies and revenue optimization approach across the Qiddiya City operating model. The role provides city-wide coordination and assurance across Estate Management, City Operations, Asset

Management, Finance, districts, operators and delivery teams to ensure operational costs, common area services and shared infrastructure are appropriately understood, allocated and recoverable where applicable.The role acts as the owner and custodian of the city-wide service charge model, providing governance, oversight and assurance over cost allocation methodologies, cost recovery structures and service charge assumptions. The position also leads the identification and evaluation of revenue opportunities across city assets, facilities, infrastructure and common areas, ensuring opportunities are assessed from operational, commercial and asset-management perspectives before recommendations are escalated to senior management. The role directs the Service Charges & Revenue Senior Manager and works closely with Lifecycle Planning, Finance, Asset Management, City Operations and district stakeholders to support long-term operational sustainability, financial resilience and value optimization across the city operating model.

Key Responsibilities

1. Service Charge Framework and Governance

• Establish and maintain the city-wide service charge framework, governance structure, policies, methodologies and

operating principles across applicable assets, facilities, services and districts.

• Develop and maintain service charge allocation principles, recharge methodologies, cost categorization structures and

governance requirements.

commercial objectives.

review and approval.

• Ensure service charge approaches remain aligned with operating models, asset ownership structures, operational

responsibilities and district requirements.

• Promote consistency in charging practices and cost recovery principles across the wider city operating model.

• Provide leadership reporting on service charge governance effectiveness, risks, issues and improvement opportunities.

2. City-Wide Service Charge Model Ownership

• Own and maintain the city-wide service charge model and supporting governance arrangements.

• Coordinate inputs from Asset Management, City Operations, Finance, districts, operators and external advisors to ensure

model integrity and consistency.

• Review and challenge charging assumptions, allocation methodologies, cost drivers and model outputs to ensure robust

decision making.

• Ensure common area services, shared infrastructure, public realm assets and city-wide services are appropriately

reflected within service charge calculations.

• Maintain transparent assumptions, supporting evidence and governance records for all significant model decisions.

• Monitor model effectiveness and ensure assumptions evolve in line with city growth, asset commissioning and operational

maturity.

• Develop management information, dashboards and reporting outputs to support leadership review and decision making.

• Support periodic reviews of service charge affordability, allocation fairness and cost recovery effectiveness.

3. Revenue Strategy and Commercial Opportunity Assessment

• Lead the identification and evaluation of revenue-generating opportunities associated with city assets, infrastructure,

facilities, services and common areas.

• Assess emerging opportunities that support operational sustainability and maximize value from city-owned or city-

managed assets.

• Coordinate commercial evaluations of potential revenue streams, recovery mechanisms and value-generation initiatives.

• Develop business case inputs, financial assessments and strategic recommendations for leadership consideration.

• Ensure revenue opportunities are evaluated against operational requirements, customer experience expectations and

long-term city objectives.

• Maintain visibility of revenue-generating initiatives across districts, operators and asset portfolios.

• Monitor market developments and emerging trends that may create future revenue opportunities for the city.

• Provide evidence-based recommendations regarding potential revenue generation, value optimization and cost recovery

enhancement.

4. OPEX and Lifecycle Cost Integration

• Coordinate operating expenditure inputs with City Operations, operators, Finance and Asset Management stakeholders.

• Ensure service charge assumptions appropriately reflect approved service levels, operational requirements and operating

delivery models.

• Work closely with the Asset Lifecycle Planning & Integration Director to incorporate lifecycle forecasts, renewal obligations

and long-term asset funding requirements into service charge considerations.

• Ensure lifecycle cost impacts and renewal pressures are visible during service charge reviews and cost recovery

assessments.

• Coordinate discussions regarding maintenance obligations, service standards, lifecycle exposure and cost allocation

assumptions.

• Challenge cost assumptions where opportunities exist to improve efficiency, affordability or value for money.

• Support integrated planning through clear visibility of operational expenditure, lifecycle obligations and recovery

opportunities.

• Promote alignment between operational sustainability objectives and cost recovery strategies.

5. Financial Assurance and Cost Recovery Performance

• Maintain a consolidated city-wide view of operational costs, service charge assumptions, recovery methodologies and

cost allocation structures.

• Review cost recovery performance and identify variances, risks, affordability issues, recovery gaps and potential revenue

leakage.

• Coordinate assurance activities relating to service charge calculations, allocation methodologies and recovery

assumptions.

• Provide recommendations to improve transparency, accountability and effectiveness of cost recovery arrangements.

• Support leadership reporting on cost recovery performance, service charge outcomes and operational affordability

pressures.

• Monitor trends, exceptions and performance indicators to identify emerging risks and improvement opportunities.

• Ensure service charge arrangements remain sustainable and support long-term operational and financial objectives.

• Develop governance reporting and performance dashboards covering cost recovery effectiveness and financial resilience.

6. District, Operator and Stakeholder Interface

• Build strong working relationships with districts, operators, City Operations, Asset Management, Finance and governance

stakeholders.

• Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities associated with service charges, revenue generation and cost recovery

initiatives.

Facilitate discussions on operating assumptions, service levels, allocation methodologies, charging structures and

recovery mechanisms.

• Ensure district and operator requirements are captured, reviewed and appropriately reflected within service charge

governance arrangements.

• Support resolution of service charge and cost allocation issues through structured engagement, analysis and

recommendations.

• Promote transparency and understanding of charging methodologies and governance requirements across stakeholders.

• Support senior leadership engagement on financially significant recovery, charging and revenue matters.

• Facilitate cross-functional reviews of emerging operational, commercial and cost recovery challenges.

7. Consultant and Commercial Management

• Define scopes, deliverables, acceptance criteria and performance requirements for consultants supporting service charge

and revenue initiatives.

• Manage consultant activities, outputs, recommendations and reporting requirements.

• Review benchmarking studies, financial assessments, charge methodologies, governance recommendations and

commercial evaluations.

• Ensure consultant outputs are evidence-based, practical and aligned with Estate Management objectives.

• Coordinate independent reviews and specialist assessments as required to support decision making.

• Escalate significant findings, risks, opportunities and recommendations to senior management where appropriate.

• Ensure consultant recommendations are translated into practical governance improvements and decision-support

outputs.

• Promote effective knowledge transfer and capability development through external specialist engagements.

8. Continuous Improvement, Benchmarking and Reporting

• Promote continual improvement of service charge governance, cost recovery methodologies and revenue opportunity

assessment processes.

• Coordinate benchmarking exercises through specialist consultants to compare service charge practices, cost recovery

arrangements and revenue opportunities against relevant market comparators.

• Monitor industry developments, regulatory changes, operational trends and emerging practices that may impact service

charge or revenue strategies.

• Develop dashboards, management reports and executive briefings covering service charge performance, revenue

opportunities and recovery effectiveness.

• Review governance effectiveness and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, transparency and value creation.

• Support the development of Estate Management capability through guidance, workshops, governance routines and

stakeholder engagement.

• Maintain lessons learned and continuous improvement processes for service charge and revenue management activities.

• Promote evidence-based decision making through high-quality reporting and performance analysis.

Requirements

Experience

• Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in service charges, commercial management, cost recovery, financial

planning, real estate operations, asset management, infrastructure operations or related disciplines, including senior leadership experience.

• Proven experience developing, managing or governing service charge models and cost allocation methodologies within

complex multi-stakeholder environments.

• Experience evaluating revenue opportunities, commercial initiatives, cost recovery strategies and financial sustainability

programs.

• Experience coordinating operational, asset management and finance stakeholders to develop evidence-based

commercial recommendations.

• Experience managing consultants, specialist advisors and commercial studies.

• Experience supporting executive-level decision making through financial modelling, governance reporting and commercial

analysis.

• Experience within large-scale destinations, cities, infrastructure programs, mixed-use developments, public realm

environments or giga-projects is strongly preferred.

Preferred Background

infrastructure finance, revenue optimization or operational finance.

environments.

operating models and commercial outcomes.

Technical & Functional Expectations

Education

Commercial Management or a related discipline.

management, real estate or business management is desirable.

jobs.title: Sr. Construction Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Senior Construction Manager (PMC) – Complex Tunnelling Projects

Position Summary

The Senior Construction Manager acts as the PMC's lead representative for construction

delivery, providing strategic oversight and assurance for major tunnelling and underground

infrastructure projects. The role is responsible for monitoring, coordinating, and managing

Cost Plus, Re-measurable, EPC/Design & Build contractors to ensure construction

activities are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with project objectives,

contractual requirements, quality standards, and regulatory obligations.

The position requires industry-leading experience in the delivery of large, technically

challenging tunnelling projects, including TBM, NATM/SEM, deep shafts, caverns,

underground premium facilities, and associated high-end habitable spaces, utility and

infrastructure works.

Key Responsibilities

Construction Leadership & Oversight

• Serve as the PMC's senior construction representative and trusted advisor to the

Client.

• Provide strategic oversight of all tunnelling and underground construction activities.

• Monitor contractor performance against approved schedules, budgets, safety

requirements, and quality objectives.

• Review and validate construction methodologies, work plans, sequencing

strategies, and resource deployment plans.

• Ensure project delivery aligns with approved project execution plans and client

objectives.

Contractor Management

Design & Build, and specialist tunnelling contractors.

• Assess contractor capabilities, productivity, performance trends, and recovery

strategies.

• Challenge and validate contractor schedules, progress reporting, risk assessments,

and mitigation plans.

• Monitor critical construction interfaces and resolve issues impacting project

delivery.

Technical Assurance

• Provide expert guidance on tunnelling methodologies and underground

construction techniques.

o TBM (micro and other) excavation works

o NATM/SEM/VMT tunnelling

o Drill and blast operations

o Shaft and cavern construction

o Ground Support, improvement and stabilization

Health, Safety and Environmental Governance
